acceptance.given: The Candidate Route has been enabled and the frozen disable fixture set and Prior Behavior Baseline are bound to the same current replay identity.

oracle.expected: For every applicable disable fixture, the real Consumer invokes the Prior Route and the recorded Prior Route identity, verdict, and diagnostic category exactly match the bound Prior Behavior Baseline; the transition reaches the stated disable postcondition.
forbidden: Disable only changes configuration or route state without a Prior Route invocation.
Any applicable fixture is omitted from disable execution.
Disable succeeds when Prior Route identity, verdict, or diagnostic category differs from the Prior Behavior Baseline.
oracle.observable: A runtime disable-transition receipt records one real Prior Route invocation per applicable fixture, fixture identity, Prior Route identity, verdict, diagnostic category, and an equality check against the Prior Behavior Baseline.

acceptance.then: Execute the bound disable transition through the real Consumer and evaluate the per-fixture Prior Route postcondition.
acceptance.when: The enabled Candidate Route is disabled.

failure_intents.selector_intent: A disable execution that omits a Prior Route invocation, omits an applicable fixture, or records a Prior Route identity, verdict, or diagnostic category different from the Prior Behavior Baseline must produce an unsuccessful disable result.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Implement and verify disable as a real Consumer invocation of the Prior Route for every applicable fixture, with per-fixture equality to the Prior Behavior Baseline identity, verdict, and diagnostic category; configuration-only switching and omitted fixtures remain unsuccessful.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing replay receipt and route-transition contracts; disable remains repository-relative, bounded, non-authorizing, and compatible with existing Consumer callers while adding the Prior Route postcondition.

slice_hint.state_transition: Candidate Route enabled -> real Consumer invokes Prior Route for each applicable fixture -> per-fixture identity/verdict/diagnostic comparison -> disable succeeds only when all comparisons match the Prior Behavior Baseline.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The disable transition is terminally successful only when every applicable fixture has a recorded real Prior Route invocation and all three Prior Behavior Baseline fields match; any omitted fixture, configuration-only transition, identity mismatch, verdict mismatch, diagnostic-category mismatch, timeout, or infrastructure failure is unsuccessful.
